OTHER PRESENT:
 SR PP SMT SEETHA S  THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 10.10.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2024:KER:75554 BAIL APPL. NO. 7093 OF 2024  3  Dated this the 10th day of October, 2024  ORDER
The application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for an order of pre-arrest bail.

2. The petitioners are the accused 1 to 4 in Crime No.792//2024 of the Kunnicode Police Station,
Kollam, which is registered against them for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 324 and 294(b) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
3.The prosecution case, in brief, is that: the first accused is the husband of the de facto complainant.
Their marriage was solemnized on 27.11.2011.
Their marital relationship is strained.
The accused 2 and 3 are the parents of the first accused and the 4th accused is the paternal uncle of the first accused.
On 17.06.2024, the first accused 2024:KER:75554 BAIL APPL. NO. 7093 OF 2024 assaulted the de facto complainant with a scissors and attempted to murder her.
She suffered grievous injuries.
The second accused abused the de facto complainant in obscene language and the accused 3 and 4 assisted the accused 1 and 2 to commit the above offences.
The accused also misappropriated the property of the de facto complainant.
Thus, the accused have committed the above offences.

sentences.text:
Heard; Smt.Anjana Kannath, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Smt. Seetha S,
the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are totally innocent of the accusations levelled against them.
There is no material to substantiate the petitioners' culpability in the crime.
The Investigating Officer has deliberately incorporated Section 498A of the IPC, to see that the petitioners are arrested.
The first petitioner and the de facto complainant were married in 2011.
2024:KER:75554 BAIL APPL. NO. 7093 OF 2024
The fact that the present FIR is registered after 14 years of the marriage, proves the falsity in the crime.
The de facto complainant has not suffered any serious injuries as alleged by the prosecution.
The petitioners 2 to 4 are senior citizens, aged above 65 years.
The petitioners are law-abiding citizens without any criminal antecedents.

The petitioners'
custodial interrogation is not necessary, and no recovery is to be effected.
Hence, the application may be allowed.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the application.
She submitted that the investigation is in progress.
She also stated that if the petitioners are granted an order of pre-arrest bail, it may hamper the investigation.

She made available the Accident Register cum Wound Certificate of the de facto complainant dated 17.06.2024 issued by the Taluk Head Quarters Hospital, Punalur, to establish the injuries suffered by the de facto complainant.
She prayed the application may be dismissed.
The prosecution case is that, the petitioners had mentally and physically harassed the de facto complainant and the first accused assaulted her with a scissors.

On a perusal of the Accident Register cum Wound Certificate referred to above, prima facie, I find that the de facto complainant only suffered abrasions over right middle finger and abrasion on her right wrist.
Moreover, even though the marriage between first petitioner and the de facto complainant was solemnized on 27.11.2011, Annexure A1 FIR is registered only on 9.7.2024.
Indisputably, the marital relationship is strained.

8. In Bhadres Bipinbhai Sheth vs State of Gujarat and another [2015 KHC 4579], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has succinctly culled out the principles for the purpose of grant of an order of pre-arrest bail in offences of a similar nature, by holding that the complaint made against the accused has to be thoroughly examined at the stage of considering a bail 2024:KER:75554 BAIL APPL. NO. 7093 OF 2024 application, especially to find out if it is a false or frivolous complaint.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The courts should examine whether there is any family dispute between the parties and whether the Investigating Officer is acting in connivance with the complainant.
The gravity of each charge and the exact role of the accused should also be properly comprehended.

The discretion to grant an order of pre-arrest bail must be exercised on the basis of the available materials and the facts of the particular case and there is no requirement that the accused must make out a special case to exercise the power of grant of anticipatory bail.

The discretion of the Court should be exercised with due care Shyju Lukose vs State Of Kerala on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116335247/
3 and circumspection, and the frivolity in the prosecution should be examined, particularly whether any harassment, humiliation or unjustified detention of the accused.

sentences.text: 9. After bestowing my anxious consideration to the facts, the materials placed on record, and the rival 2024:KER:75554 BAIL APPL. NO. 7093 OF 2024 submissions made across the Bar, and taking note of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the afore-cited decision, and on considering the fact that the marital relationship between the first petitioner and the de facto complainant is strained and there are disputes pending between them, and further that there is a delay in registering the FIR, I am satisfied and convinced that the petitioners have made out valid grounds to invoke the discretionary jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the BNS.

Hence,
I am inclined to allow the application, but subject to stringent conditions.
They shall then appear before the Investigating Officer, as and when directed;
